device.category: hybrid synthesiser: digital oscillator, analog filter, 4-voice paraphonic, 25-key capacitive touch keyboard, mod matrix, arpeggiator, sequencer
device.based_on: Arturia design (2019). Seven of the twelve oscillator models use Mutable Instruments Plaits code (MIT licence). Matrix concept from Arturia's MatrixBrute.

sources.title: Arturia MicroFreak User Manual, product version 1.1.2
sources.note: Revision date 20 May 2019. Covers panel, rear panel, signal flow, presets, matrix, the 12 oscillator models, filter, LFO, envelopes, keyboard, icon strip, arpeggiator, sequencer, Utility and MIDI Control Center settings, CV/gate, cheat sheet. No MIDI CC chart, no specification table.

sources.title: Arturia MicroFreak User Manual, product version 5.0.0 (6 July 2023), retailer copy
sources.note: Appendix D default CC table; Utility tables for firmware 5; parameters of the oscillator types added since 1.1.2. Used for the CC map and for firmware notes only.

sources.title: Arturia support, 'MicroFreak Allgemeine Fragen' (German FAQ)
sources.note: Same CC map with ranges (Type 10-127, free Arp/Seq rate 0-123); program change banks of 128; paraphonic per-voice envelopes; grounding.

sources.title: Arturia press releases and support notes for firmware 2.0 (Jan 2020), 2.1 (Aug 2020), 3.0 (Jan 2021), 4.0 (Oct 2021), 5.0 (2023)
sources.note: Also: arturia.com/company/press/press-releases/microfreak-receives-firmware-update-2; MusicRadar, Engadget and Synthtopia reports.

sources.title: Thomann UK, Arturia MicroFreak product page
sources.note: 311 x 233 x 55 mm, 1.02 kg; CV/gate/pressure and clock on 3.5 mm jacks; filter described as an analog state-variable design inspired by the SEM.

architecture.synthesis_note: One digital oscillator running one of 12 models (wavetable, virtual analogue, FM, granular formant, chords, speech, physical models) with three macro parameters Wave, Timbre and Shape, into an analog filter and VCA.
architecture.signal_path_note: Hybrid: digital oscillator; analog multimode filter and analog VCA; extra digital VCAs per voice in paraphonic mode. All controls are digitally scanned and saved.
architecture.polyphony_mode: Mono, or paraphonic up to 4 voices sharing one filter (Paraphonic button). Per-voice amplitude via internal digital VCA envelopes ('extended paraphony'). The Chords model disables paraphony.
architecture.patch_memory_note: 256 presets: 1-128 factory, 129-160 templates, the rest empty (Init/Bass). A preset stores knob values, matrix, both sequences with modulation tracks and Utility>Preset settings. Hold, Spice/Dice and arp patterns are not saved.
architecture.panel_counts_note: Counted from the panel images. Knobs: Master, Glide, Type, Wave, Timbre, Shape, Cutoff, Resonance, Rise, Fall, Hold, Amount, Arp/Seq Rate, LFO Rate, Attack, Decay/Rel, Sustain, Filter Amt; encoders: Matrix, Preset. Buttons: Assign1-3, Paraphonic, Panel, Save, Utility, Filter Type, Cycling Env Mode, Octave left/right, Shift, Arp|Seq, Oct|Mod, LFO Shape, Amp Mod. Touch icons: Hold, Up|A, Order|B, Rand|O (record), Pattern|> (play), Spice, Dice, Bend.
architecture.summary: Keyboard, arpeggiator, sequencer or MIDI notes go through glide to the digital oscillator; its Type, Wave, Timbre and Shape set the model and sound. The analog filter (LP/BP/HP, cutoff, resonance) is swept by the main envelope via Filter Amt; the VCA follows the key gate or, with Amp Mod on, the envelope. Five sources (cycling envelope, envelope, LFO, pressure, key/arp) reach Pitch, Wave, Timbre and Cutoff plus three assignable destinations through a 35-point bipolar matrix.

modules.name: Capacitive keyboard
modules.description: 25-key touch capacitive keyboard (2 octaves) generating gate, pitch and pressure (aftertouch or velocity per preset). Octave buttons shift +/-3 octaves; Key Hold latches notes.

modules.name: Touch strip
modules.description: Touch strip in three modes: Bend (pitch, absolute or relative), Spice (amount of gate/trigger variation), Dice (re-roll the variation).

modules.name: MIDI and USB interface
modules.description: MIDI on 3.5 mm TRS jacks (DIN adapters supplied) and class-compliant USB. Receives notes, CCs, program change, clock, start/stop and sustain; transmits keyboard notes (fully polyphonic), aftertouch, velocity, knob CCs, arp/seq notes and clock.

modules.name: Tempo clock and sync
modules.description: Internal tempo (default 120 BPM) or USB, MIDI or analog clock (One step, 2, 24 or 48 PPQ). Clock out sends clock while playing; a TRS lead also carries start.

modules.name: Arpeggiator
modules.description: Up, Order, Random or Pattern (generated semi-random patterns), range 1-4 octaves, free BPM or synced divisions, swing 50-75%. Patterns can be copied to sequence A or B.

modules.name: Sequencer
modules.description: Two paraphonic sequences (A, B) per preset, 4-64 steps (shared length), up to 4 notes, velocity and tie/rest per step, step or real-time recording, four modulation tracks recording knob values.

modules.name: Voice assignment
modules.description: Assigns keyboard, MIDI, arpeggiator and sequencer notes to 1 or 4 paraphonic voices. Keyboard and MIDI notes have priority over the sequencer; in mono a held key pauses the sequence.

modules.name: Glide
modules.description: Portamento: time (0 to about 10 s), synced divisions, or rate per octave (Utility Glide mode).

modules.name: Digital oscillator
modules.description: One oscillator running one of 12 models; Wave, Timbre and Shape are the model's three parameters. Range C-2 to G8. Wave, Timbre and Shape modulation are per voice; Type changes for all voices.

modules.name: Analog filter
modules.description: Analog 12 dB/octave multimode filter: low pass, band pass, high pass. Cutoff about 30 Hz to above 15 kHz; self-oscillates at full resonance. One filter shared by all voices.

properties.design: state variable, described by retailers as Oberheim SEM-inspired (not stated in the manual)

modules.name: VCA
modules.description: Analog VCA controlled by the key gate (Amp Mod off) or the envelope (Amp Mod on); in paraphonic mode, internal digital VCAs give each voice its own envelope copy.

modules.name: Envelope
modules.description: ADS envelope (Decay/Release on one knob): attack 0-10 s, decay/release 0-13 s, sustain level. Hardwired to cutoff through bipolar Filter Amt and, with Amp Mod, to the VCA. Polyphonic as a matrix source.

modules.name: Cycling envelope
modules.description: Rise, Fall and Hold/Sustain with shapeable Rise and Fall curves (Shift; log-linear-exp) and output Amount. Modes: Env (one-shot, sustains while held), Run (free-running, reset by MIDI start), Loop (cycling, reset by each trigger).

modules.name: LFO
modules.description: Six shapes (sine, triangle, saw up, square, random stepped, random gliding). Free 0.06-100 Hz or synced 8/1 to 1/32. Optional retrigger per preset.

modules.name: Matrix assignable columns
modules.description: The three assignable matrix columns: each sums its five source points and drives the parameter chosen for that column (almost any knob, or another matrix point's amount).

modules.name: Output
modules.description: Mono line output (balanced TRS) and headphone output, both after Master volume; per-preset relative volume.

modules.name: CV/Gate/Pressure outputs
modules.description: Pitch (1 V/oct, Hz/V or 1.2 V/oct), gate (S-trig, V-trig 5 V or 12 V) and pressure or velocity (1-10 V range). Sequencer: a step's lowest note; keyboard: the last note played.

modules.name: Display, presets and global controls
modules.panel_section: display / Preset / Save / Utility / Panel / Shift
modules.description: OLED display, Preset encoder, Save, Utility menus, Panel (apply current knob positions), Shift.

parameters.label: Type

values.label: BasicWaves
values.meaning: Arturia. Wave = Morph: square to saw to two saws; Timbre = Sym: pulse width or phase between the two saws (no effect at saw, Wave 50); Shape = Sub: sine sub-oscillator.

values.label: SuperWave
values.meaning: Arturia. Wave: waveform to multiply (saw, square, triangle, sine); Timbre = Detune; Shape = Volume of the detuned copies.

values.label: Wavetable
values.meaning: Arturia. Wave = Table (16 tables); Timbre = Position (32 cycles of 256 samples); Shape = Chorus.

values.label: Harmo
values.meaning: Arturia harmonic oscillator. Wave = Content (harmonic amplitude tables); Timbre = Sculpting (sine to triangle partials); Shape = Chorus.

values.label: KarplusStr
values.meaning: Arturia Karplus-Strong. Wave = Bow (continuous excitation); Timbre = Position (strike position/strength); Shape = Decay.

values.label: V.Analog
values.meaning: Plaits. Wave = Detune between two waves; Timbre = Shape (narrow pulse to square to hard-sync formants); Shape = Wave (triangle to saw with widening notch).

values.label: Waveshaper
values.meaning: Plaits. Wave = waveshaper waveform; Timbre = wavefolder Amount; Shape = Asym (asymmetry).

values.label: Two Op.FM
values.meaning: Plaits. Wave = Ratio; Timbre = Amount (modulation index); Shape = feedback (operator 2 self-modulation).

values.label: Formant
values.meaning: Plaits granular formant. Wave = Interval (formant 1:2 ratio); Timbre = Formant frequency; Shape = formant width and shape.

values.label: Chords
values.meaning: Plaits, four-voice chord oscillator (disables paraphony; last key is the root). Wave = Type (octave, 5th, sus4, m, m7, m9, m11, 6/9, M9, M7, M); Timbre = Inv/Transp; Shape = Waveform (string-machine waves, then a 16-wave table).

values.label: Speech
values.meaning: Plaits vowel and speech. Wave = Type (formants up to about 100, then libraries of colours, numbers, letters, words); Timbre = formant shift; Shape = Word within the library.

values.label: Modal
values.meaning: Plaits modal resonator. Wave = Inharm (inharmonicity / material); Timbre = excitation brightness and dust density; Shape = Decay (damping).

parameters.function: Oscillator model; each value lists what Wave, Timbre and Shape do. Can be modulated (all voices change together).

behaviours.name: Preset vs knob position
behaviours.rule: After loading, knob positions don't match the sound; a moved knob joins the preset per Knob catch (Jump, Hook, Scaled). Panel applies all current positions at once.

behaviours.name: Matrix sums
behaviours.rule: Several sources on one destination add; all points are bipolar (-100 to +100); negative cutoff modulation can silence the sound.

behaviours.name: Hardwired routes
behaviours.rule: Key pitch to oscillator, envelope to cutoff (Filter Amt = the Env > Cutoff point) and envelope or gate to the VCA are built in; Key/Arp > Pitch scales the existing tracking (larger or microtonal steps).

behaviours.name: Assign columns
behaviours.rule: Hold Assign1-3 and move a knob to set the column's destination for all five sources; hold Assign and pick a matrix point to modulate that point's amount.

behaviours.name: Paraphony
behaviours.rule: Up to 4 voices share the analog filter; each has its own internal VCA envelope copy. Polyphonic sources (envelope, pressure, key/arp, arpeggiator) modulate Wave, Timbre and Shape per voice; Type changes for all voices.

behaviours.name: Chords model
behaviours.rule: Selecting Chords disables paraphony: the last key is the root and one chord plays.

behaviours.name: Note priority
behaviours.rule: Keyboard and MIDI notes take voices before the sequencer; with paraphony off only a step's lowest note plays; in mono a held key pauses the sequence.

behaviours.name: Amp Mod
behaviours.rule: Amp Mod off: the VCA follows the gate (arp/seq gate length is audible). On: the envelope shapes the volume.

behaviours.name: Cycling envelope modes
behaviours.rule: Env runs once; Run free-runs (reset by MIDI start); Loop cycles and resets on each trigger. In Run and Loop, Hold is a hold time; in Env it is a sustain level.

behaviours.name: Spice and Dice
behaviours.rule: Spice morphs each step's gate from the default length to a random 'status'; Dice rolls a new status. They also nudge octave, velocity and amp release. Not saved.

behaviours.name: Arp octave buttons
behaviours.rule: Octave buttons during an arpeggio add new notes in the new range rather than transposing the running arpeggio.

behaviours.name: Arp to sequence
behaviours.rule: Shift + Up|A or Order|B copies the current arpeggio to sequence A or B, extended to the sequence length.

behaviours.name: Mod tracks
behaviours.rule: Up to four knobs per preset; touching a knob in step record assigns it to the next free track; a fifth shows 'Memory full'. Tracks are shared by sequences A and B.

behaviours.name: Sequence auto-play
behaviours.rule: With a recorded sequence, pressing a key starts it without pressing play.

behaviours.name: CV output note
behaviours.rule: Only one pitch CV: a sequence step sends its lowest note, the keyboard the last note played. MIDI carries all notes, including chords beyond four.

behaviours.name: Clock out
behaviours.rule: While playing, MIDI clock and analog clock are sent; play/stop sends MIDI start/stop.

behaviours.name: Hold and MIDI
behaviours.rule: Key Hold does not latch external MIDI notes; send sustain instead.

behaviours.name: Power
behaviours.rule: USB (5 V 500 mA) or 12 V DC; plugging in DC resets the unit; the keyboard needs the grounded supplied adapter to work properly.

midi.note: The 1.1.2 manual has no CC chart. CC numbers come from the default CC table in the v5.0 manual (Appendix D) and Arturia's support FAQ, which agree; they are assumed to apply to earlier firmware. All CCs 0-127 except Type (10-127) and free Arp/Seq rate (0-123). Free and synced rates have separate CCs: 91/92 Arp/Seq, 93/94 LFO. On firmware 5, Type values per model are spread across 0-127 for 22 models (forum measurements); the 12-model ranges for 1.1.2 are not published. Matrix amounts, buttons and Utility settings have no CCs. Program change: bank of 128 presets per bank select (1-128, 129-256).

firmware_history.2.0: January 2020: Noise oscillator (particle, white, metallic); Chord Mode (hold Paraphonic and play a chord); scale quantise; copy sequence A to B; Shift + long press Matrix clears all routings; 64 presets
firmware_history.2.1: August 2020: Vocoder oscillator (16-band; mic via TRRS headset in the headphone socket); Vocoder Edition hardware
firmware_history.3.0: January 2021: Noise Engineering Bass, Harm and SawX oscillators; 4-voice unison (spread up to 12 semitones, modulatable); 384 presets; last preset recalled at power-on
firmware_history.4.0: October 2021: WaveUser oscillator (user wavetables via MIDI Control Center); 64 presets
firmware_history.5.0: May-July 2023: Sample, Scan Grains, Cloud Grains and Hit Grains oscillators; 512 presets; Key/Arp Random mode; Envelope Snap; reorganised Utility (Unison Count 2-4, Unison Spread, Scale and Root, Osc Knob Speed, mic settings)
firmware_history.note: This file models the 12 oscillator types and settings of 1.1.2. Firmware 5 has 22 types: those here plus Noise, Bass, SawX, Harm, WaveUser, Sample, Scan Grains, Cloud Grains, Hit Grains and Vocoder.

source_inconsistencies: LFO range: '0.05Hz up to 100Hz' (p.15) versus 0.06 Hz to 100 Hz (p.50, twice).
Bend range: Utility table 0-24, 'zero to two octaves' (p.24, p.83) versus default 24 steps (12 each side) with a maximum of 48 steps, four octaves (p.66).
The envelope reset setting is 'Envelope legato' (p.24 table, p.82 text) and 'Envelope reset' (p.54 note, p.83 table).
Envelope Filter Amount is described in the destination and mod-track tables as 'the amount of signal sent from Envelope to AMP'; everywhere else it sets envelope to cutoff.
Gate format: 'V-Trig 12V' in the Utility and MCC tables (p.84, p.87) versus 'V-Trig 10V' in the CV chapter (p.92).
Headphones: '3.5 mm TRS jack' (p.7) versus 'standard 3.5 mm TS or TRS jack' (p.18).
Mem protect options: 'Off / Factory only / On' (Utility table) versus 'Off, Factory only, All' (MCC section).
Knob catch: the MCC section says the knobs are '360-degree encoders', while Hook and Jump modes and the rest of the manual treat them as absolute knobs.
Paraphonic: 'depending on the number of voices you have specified in Utility' (p.21), but no voice-count setting appears in the Utility tables.
Swing: 'Hold SHIFT and turn the Rate encoder' versus 'hold the blue SHIFT button and press Rate' (both p.70).
LFO sync: '8/1 ... completes in 8 pulses, which is 1/4 of a quarter note' (p.50) contradicts 8/1 being its slowest (eight-bar) rate.
Pitch range: 'the whole pitch range is eight octaves' (p.61) versus the oscillator range C-2 to G8 (p.35).
Cross references: the Shift section points to the arpeggiator as chapter 12 [p.72] and the sequencer as chapter 13 [p.67]; the page numbers are swapped.
Sequencer mode is said to change 'the first five icons'; the strip has Hold plus four arp/seq icons, and the Arp list names 'Hold' where Up is meant (p.73).
The CV 0 V reference text says 'when pitch format is set to 0V/Oct' (p.87); the table says 1 V/Oct or 1.2 V/Oct.
Assignable destinations list Arp&Seq Rate; the modulation-track table omits it (otherwise the lists match).
Between sources: A reference range 427.4-452.89 Hz (1.1.2) versus 427.47-453.89 Hz (v5 manual).
Between sources: the v5 manual repeats the LFO inconsistency with three values (0.05 Hz, 0.1 Hz, 0.06 Hz); 0.06 Hz is used.
Between sources: the cheat sheet in circulation gives default gate length 10-90% (default 50%); both manuals say 5-85% (default 45%).
Between sources: on firmware 5 the CC 9 value the MicroFreak transmits for several oscillator types falls outside the range it accepts for that type (forum report).

modelling_gaps.detail: The fixed 5 x 7 grid is modelled as one amount parameter per point and connections, not the slot-based mod_matrix section (which assumes selectable sources). Assign columns route through module 'mx' with switched connections by target.
An Assign column can target another point's amount; the chosen point is not representable, only the 'matrix_point' target value.
Per-voice modulation of Wave/Timbre/Shape by polyphonic sources versus common Type and filter is described in module scope and behaviours only.
The manual gives display scales only through examples; ranges marked 0-100 are inferred.
Notes, ties, velocities and the four recorded knob tracks are sequence content, not parameters; only settings are modelled.
The schema has only analogue or digital; recorded as digital with a hybrid note (digital oscillator, analog filter and VCA). A hybrid value is worth adding in 0.14.0.
